title: Ethiopian Berbere Fries
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Berbere Fries — thick-cut potato fries seasoned with a berbere-salt blend and mitmita immediately after frying. The Ethiopian answer to seasoned fries — where ordinary chips become something extraordinary with the berbere spice tradition.
longDesc: Berbere fries are the simplest expression of the modern Ethiopian food identity — the globally ubiquitous French fry, transformed by the application of berbere-salt at the moment of coming out of the oil, into something distinctly and completely Ethiopian.
ingredients: 600g potatoes — peeled, cut into thick batons
// Berbere Salt: 1 tbsp berbere (ETH141) + 1 tsp salt + ¼ tsp mitmita (ETH142)
steps: Soak potato batons in cold water 30 minutes. Dry thoroughly.
First fry: 160°C for 5 minutes. Remove. Cool 10 minutes.
Second fry: 190°C for 3—4 minutes until very crispy.
Drain. Immediately toss in berbere salt while hot.
chefTips: Double-frying is essential for crispy fries.
Season while hot — the berbere salt adheres to the oil surface.
Mitmita adds a fierce finishing heat — use judiciously.
cookingScience: Double-frying: the first low-temperature fry dehydrates the interior (gelatinising the starch and evaporating moisture). The second high-temperature fry creates the crispy shell through rapid surface dehydration and Maillard browning.
culturalNote: Berbere fries are the Addis Ababa café's most ordered side dish — the combination of crispy potato with berbere and mitmita seasoning produces a flavour that is completely familiar (fries) and completely Ethiopian (berbere) simultaneously.
